title: Tracing Stereotypes in Pre-trained Transformers: From Biased Neurons to Fairer Models
findings: Stereotypical knowledge related to religion, like other biases, was found to be encoded in small, distinct, and highly localized subsets of neurons. Suppressing these neurons effectively reduced the model's tendency to generate stereotypical content. However, in the downstream Software Engineering (SE) task evaluation, suppressing neurons associated with religion stereotypes (category BR07) caused one of the largest performance drops in the macro-F1 score for classification tasks, though the overall degradation was still considered small.

measurement_description: Detection of stereotypical associations related to religious groups. The study created a dataset of 'biased relations' (stereotypes) for nine categories, including religion, and then identified and suppressed the specific 'biased neurons' in models that encode these stereotypes.
